passage.title: 'The Lens', teacher-written modern travel writing for TGA
paras: The lighthouse keeper's cottage is a museum now. You pay at a little window and climb the same hundred and twelve steps he climbed each night, though nobody makes you do it in a gale. At the top, behind glass, sits the great lens: a beehive of prisms taller than a man, so clean it seems to hold the sky. A card explains how it turned on a bath of mercury, so smoothly that a child could push it. I did push it, very gently, when the guide was not looking. It moved. Somewhere, two hundred years of ships seemed to move with it.

model.title: How does the writer use language and structure to make the visit memorable?

parts.text: Language 1: metaphor 'a beehive of prisms' (scale, wonder)
Language 2: 'so clean it seems to hold the sky' (awe)
Structure: ordinary start (paying at a window) to a private moment
Ending: 'two hundred years of ships seemed to move with it' (history felt)

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A four-line plan: two language points, one structural point, the ending.

keywords.def: find and copy or paraphrase precise information
work out what is suggested, not stated
explain how the writer's choices create effects
judge how well something works, with reasons

questions.q: Q1 and Q2 style: what is the lens 'taller than'? What did it turn on?
questions.a: a man; a bath of mercury

questions.q: Q5 style: give two things the writer tells us about the lens
questions.a: any two: a beehive of prisms; taller than a man; very clean; turned on mercury; a child could push it

questions.q: Core (timed, 12 minutes): in the portal response box, answer the 10-mark question from the model plan. Starter: 'The writer makes the visit memorable by...'
questions.a: Mark scheme points: 'beehive of prisms' (scale and pattern); 'hold the sky' (awe); contrast of the tourist window with the keeper's gales; the secret push as a turning point; the final sentence's leap across 'two hundred years'. Top answers weave language and structure with effects.

questions.q: Extend: self-mark against the ladder and write one target
questions.a: A level and a precise target.

questions.q: Stretch: rewrite your weakest sentence so the effect leads
Which is the best answer to 'How many steps does the writer climb?'
options: lots of steps up the tower
the same steps as the keeper did in a gale
questions.a: A) a hundred and twelve. One precise detail earns the mark; extra words risk errors.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: where should my minutes go?
questions.a: Most to Q3, Q6 and Q7; short questions fast.
